title: The fog stays out
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: A heat wave, inland. On the coast the fog stays out and the town gets the leftover: eighty degrees, which nobody owns a shirt for. Wood in the overcoat. Gully in the hoodie. The uncle in the chair with a wet towel. The strip sweats in the line.

panels.composition: Main street in unusual heat: the fog a wall offshore, the street in full sun, people in the wrong clothes. WOOD in the overcoat. BARNABY flat on the sidewalk.

image.prompt: a small coastal town's main street in bright unfamiliar heat with a wall of fog offshore, a young man in a heavy overcoat, a small dog lying flat on the sidewalk, black and white, no words

panels.composition: Wood, sweating, not taking the coat off.

image.prompt: a young man sweating in a heavy wool overcoat, refusing to remove it, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The shack. GULLY in the hoodie. The UNCLE in the chair with a wet towel on his head, the oxygen line, unremarked.

image.prompt: a teenager in a hoodie and an old man in a lawn chair with a wet towel on his head in bright heat beside a shack, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The town in heat. Everyone wrong for it. The line shaky — the strip says it's the heat. The strip said it was cold in January. The strip has a reason for every line.

notes: Eighty degrees; nobody owns a shirt for it. The line: the heat, this time.
